properties.areaDesc: York, VA; City of Hampton, VA; City of Newport News, VA; City of Poquoson, VA
properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued November 26 at 10:15AM EST until November 26 at 10:45AM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
TORAKQ

The National Weather Service in Wakefield has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
York County in southeastern Virginia...
The City of Hampton in southeastern Virginia...
The Northern City of Newport News in southeastern Virginia...
The City of Poquoson in southeastern Virginia...

* Until 1045 AM EST.

* At 1015 AM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
tornado was located 2 miles south of Fort Monroe, moving northwest
at 55 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* This tornado will be near...
Hampton, Buckroe Beach, Hampton University, Grand View, Hampton
River Inlet, Fort Monroe, Hampton Flats, Northampton and Hampton
Roads Bridge Tunnel around 1020 AM EST.
Poquoson, Langley AFB and Newport News around 1025 AM EST.
Seaford, Tabb and Patrick Henry Field around 1030 AM EST.

Other locations impacted by the tornado include Langley View, Fox
Hill, Phoebus, Raleigh Terrace, Messick, Plum Tree Island Refuge,
Dare, Oriana, Hornsbyville and Harris Grove.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Heavy rainfall is hiding this tornado. Do not wait to see or hear the
tornado. Take cover now!

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 26 at 10:11AM EST until November 26 at 10:45AM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
SMWAKQ

The National Weather Service in Wakefield has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Chesapeake Bay from New Point Comfort to Little Creek VA...
James River from JRB to HRBT, Including the Elizabeth River...

* Until 1045 AM EST.

* At 1011 AM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located over Thimble Shoals, or over Willoughby
Bay, moving north at 45 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts in excess of 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Boats could suffer significant structural
damage in high winds. Small craft could capsize in
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Thimble Shoals, Hampton Roads Bridge Tunnel, Hampton River Inlet,
Willoughby Bay, Bluefish Rock, Hampton Flats, Sewells Point,
Poquoson and Little Creek.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 10:09AM EST until November 26 at 4:15PM EST by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...The City of Roanoke in west central Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 415 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams continue to
rise due to excess runoff from rainfall continuing from overnight.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1003 AM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
prolonged light to moderate rainfall across the City of Roanoke.
Flooding is already occurring in the warned area. Between 2.5 and
3.5 inches of rain have fallen since late Wednesday evening.
- Some creeks and streams that have flooded out of their banks
include Peters Creek at Strauss Park, Mudlick Creek, and Murray
Run at Fishburn Park.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Roanoke and Vinton.
- For flooding safety information, please visit
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service
by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports and
pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.areaDesc: Stokes; Rockingham; Caswell; Floyd; Roanoke; Botetourt; Rockbridge; Patrick; Franklin; Bedford; Amherst; Henry; Pittsylvania; Campbell; Appomattox; Buckingham; Halifax; Charlotte
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 26 at 10:03AM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central North Carolina, including the
following counties, Caswell, Rockingham and Stokes and Virginia,
including the following counties, Amherst, Appomattox, Bedford,
Botetourt, Buckingham, Campbell, Charlotte, Floyd, Franklin,
Halifax, Henry, Patrick, Pittsylvania, Roanoke and Rockbridge.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM EST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in poor drainage flooding,
especially where leaves have filled road-side ditches, and water
gets diverted onto the highway. Stream levels were at all time lows
prior to this rain event, but still watch for sudden rises on area
creeks, streams and rivers. Also monitor for flooding in urban
areas. Storm drains may become clogged with debris causing flooding
of the surrounding area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain will be moderate to heavy at times and lead to nuisance
flooding in poor drainage and leaf clogged drains through this
evening. Widespread rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches are
expected, with localized higher totals for favored upslope
locations along the Blue Ridge from Poor Mountain near Roanoke,
northward toward the Peaks of Otter.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 8:42AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady with Major Flood
Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 4.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Thursday was 4.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.4 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
is expected.

* WHERE...Amelia County in central Virginia...
Chesterfield County in central Virginia...
Cumberland County in central Virginia...
Henrico County in central Virginia...
Powhatan County in central Virginia...
Prince Edward County in central Virginia...
The City of Colonial Heights in central Virginia...
The City of Richmond in central Virginia...
Dinwiddie County in south central Virginia...
Nottoway County in south central Virginia...
The City of Hopewell in south central Virginia...
The City of Petersburg in south central Virginia...

shortly.

Heights, Cumberland, Farmville, Blackstone, Crewe, McKenney,
Mannboro, Amelia Courthouse, Moseley, Bon Air, Tuckahoe,

Richmond.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 5:07AM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low
lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to 1 foot of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and
tidal waterways. Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted. Tide along the open coast will also be
high, but less than what was experienced Wednesday due to
reduced surf

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM PST Thursday. High tide is at 12:54
PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with isolated closures expected.
Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata
Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this event will be
higher than normal but not quite as high as the previous near
record recording from Tuesday 11/24 at 10.16 feet.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 4:34AM PST until November 27 at 9:27AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near
record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift
flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including
SR 106, and much of the farm land.   Flooding will occur all along
the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It
will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises
through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage
possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1245 PM PST.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 2:45AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Tidal levels across the panhandle are expected to be running high
for the next few days. These high tides combined with passing low
pressures and their associated fronts could create some
potentially higher than normal water levels. Confidence has
increased for a slightly weaker system moving into the panhandle
during peak tides. Tides may exceed astronomical high tide, though
the likelihood of exceeding a foot has been reduced significantly.

properties.areaDesc: Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 26 at 3:03AM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
Localized moderate to significant coastal flooding is expected
for Jalama Beach and for most coastal areas from Miramar Beach
to Rincon Point. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. Conditions
will be worse west of Point Conception, including Jalama Beach
with large breaking waves of 15 to 20 feet and moderate to
significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Until noon PST today.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. There
is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock
damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of
harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greater impacts are expected west of
Point Conception, and for most coastal areas from Miramar
Beach to Rincon Point, where damaging flooding of sea water is
more likely, especially for vulnerable low-lying coastal areas
around the time of high tide including over beaches, beach
parking lots and coastal roads. For the previously mentioned
areas, significant beach erosion is expected, powerful waves
and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean
drowning and damage to coastal structures and homes at the
waters edge. Extremely high tides of around 8.0 feet will
likely peak between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 26 at 3:03AM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large
breaking waves of 8 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon PST today.
For the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 9 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria
Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures.
Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and
strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean
drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Ventura Pier) and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact
Ventura and Channel Islands Harbors. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of around 8.1 feet
will peak between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 26 at 2:05AM PST until November 26 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides,
combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave
heights of 20 to 25 ft, will bring 2.5 to 3.0 ft of inundation
above ground level in low-lying areas and shorelines on
Thursday.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the
communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold
Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact
portions of Highway 101, especially around Coos Bay.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Roads may be closed. Low lying property including
homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be
inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be
during the highest high tide early Thursday afternoon. Storm
activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be
present, which will likely maintain inundation impacts. At the
Charleston, Oregon tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at
12:23 PM Thursday. Minor coastal flooding is also still
possible on Friday with the high tide at 1:14 PM. Tides look
to return to more typical heights over the weekend.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Newport/Morehead City has issued a

Green Mill Run At Green Mill Run in Greenville affecting Pitt
County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Green Mill Run at Green Mill Run in Greenville.

* WHEN...From early this morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.5 feet, Water likely covers portions of Charles
Boulevard adjacent to the stream. The driveway for Bower Apartments

impassable. Water also spreads to portions of Ficklen Drive and
Deck Street, and inundates portions of ECU College Hill parking
lot.

- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:40 AM EST Thursday was 7.7 feet.
- Forecast...No forecast is available for this location.
- Flood stage is 7.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 7.7
feet on 08/31/2024.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at water.weather.gov/ahps.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon by 500 PM EST.

properties.areaDesc: Southeast Suffolk
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 26 at 4:33AM EST until November 27 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Northeast Suffolk and Southeast Suffolk Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday
morning through Friday afternoon.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including
roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses
with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are
likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also
extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result
in widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of
high tide. There is potential for localized overwashes
resulting in some flooding of roadways and vulnerable
structures behind protective dunes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Higher than forecast water levels are possible
with the Friday morning high tide as storm force winds shift
from easterly today to southwesterly gales Friday morning. This could
cause seiching of the higher water over the western Great South Bay
into the eastern Great South Bay for the Friday AM high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 25 at 11:54PM PST until November 27 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.5 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
F For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker
waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 26 at 1:25AM EST until November 27 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and rough
surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST this
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: The Coastal Flood Watch has been replaced. Please see the latest information from NWS Eureka CA on this developing situation.
properties.description: The Coastal Flood Watch has been replaced. Please see the latest information from NWS Eureka CA on this developing situation.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:07PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

morning.

Putnam counties in southeastern New York.

* IMPACTS...Minor to locally moderate tidal flooding is expected
along the river around the times of high tide.

- At 416 PM EST, Water levels along the Hudson River will increase
to minor and locally moderate thresholds during the times of high
tide Thursday morning through Friday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
